minutes.headline: Zoning board granted all three special permits: Peninsula Drive rebuild, Spring Street rebuild, and an auto upholstery shop.
minutes.summary: The Zoning Board of Appeals heard three special permit applications. It granted a rebuild at 178 Peninsula Drive, a rebuild of a fire-damaged house at 5 Spring Street, and a custom upholstery and light auto repair shop at 321 Willam Road. The board set conditions on each; the shop's conditions include a 20-foot setback for vehicles, no winter storage and Saturday hours.

public_comment.topic: Neighbor on Peninsula Drive in favor of tearing down the dilapidated house at 178 Peninsula Drive.
Neighbor opposed to the auto shop: noise from past business, safety near the playground, traffic, chemical contamination, Saturday morning hours.
Character reference for the applicant, a former student and employee; says the work is artisan and low volume.
Neutral; concerned the notice did not mention boats and asked how long boats would stay, including over winter.
Character reference for the applicant, a friend.
Concern that boats parked in front would block sight lines at Hamlin Street and Willam Road.
Asked that Saturday hours start later, such as 10:00.

votes.motion: Grant special permit to demolish the existing structure at 178 Peninsula Drive and rebuild a year-round home, with conditions (septic, Board of Health, water hookup, other boards).
Grant special permit to raise the existing house at 5 Spring Street and reconstruct a new house as submitted.
Grant special permit at 321 Willam Road with the conditions as discussed.

decisions.decision: Written decision due within 14 days, followed by a 20-day appeal period; the applicant was advised to record it at the registry of deeds.
Board dropped a numeric limit and time limit on outdoor vehicles at 321 Willam Road in favor of a 20-foot setback area and no winter boat storage.
Saturday hours at the Willam Road shop set at 9 to 1.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals granted a special permit to demolish and rebuild a year-round home at 178 Peninsula Drive, with conditions including septic, Board of Health and water hookup.
The board granted a special permit to raise the fire-damaged house at 5 Spring Street and build a new house as submitted.
The board granted a special permit for an upholstery and light auto repair shop at 321 Willam Road, with the conditions as discussed.
For the Willam Road shop, the board replaced a numeric and time limit on outdoor vehicles with a 20-foot setback area and no winter boat storage.
Saturday hours at the Willam Road shop were set at 9 to 1, after a neighbor asked for a later start.

why_it_matters: The Willam Road permit lets a vehicle-work business operate near homes and a playground, and its setback, winter storage and Saturday-hours conditions are what neighbors can look to for noise, traffic and sight-line limits.
The two rebuild permits change what stands at 178 Peninsula Drive and 5 Spring Street, which touches abutters on septic, water and flood-plain questions.
watch_next: Written decisions are due within 14 days of the hearing, followed by a 20-day appeal period.
Applicants were advised to record the decisions at the registry of deeds.
